title: Slot scarcity savings sketch: micro-scenarios and ascii charts
content:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch that collects short micro-scenarios where GPU slot scarcity (shortage of reserved fast-path slots) interacts with batching and fallback policies. Goal: surface cheap win tactics we can prototype in the next 2 sprints and capture simple ascii charts for product collateral. NOT final benchmarking — lots of rough edges and unanswered questions below.

Topline hypotheses (to validate):
- H1: Under moderate burstiness (1.5x baseline qps for ~30s), slot-sparing (aggressive multiplexing + short warm-pool) can recover >30% of p99 latency without increasing $/token more than 8%.
- H2: For heavy microbursts (3–6x qps, <10s), fast preemptive tiling gives best dollar-latency tradeoff vs long prewarm; but quality risk exists for KV-heavy contexts.
- H3: Small reductions in KV cache miss penalty (10–20 ms) give outsized p90 improvements when slot contention is the bottleneck.

Experiment matrix (short):
- Hardware: A100-80GB (baseline), RTX6000 (cost proxy), and a simulated high-IO low-vram instance (for tiling tests).
- Model: 7B open-llm variant (seq_len 512), 1-pass generation token ceiling 128.
- Workloads: steady (100 qps), moderate-burst (100 -> 150 qps for 30s every 5m), microburst (100 -> 500 qps for 8–12s random).
- Policies:
  * baseline: dedicated slots (1 request per slot), on-demand prewarm (200ms), no multiplexing.
  * slot-sparing: multiplex 2x per slot, warm-pool size 10% capacity, fast-tiling fallback.
  * tiling-preempt: pack small sessions into tiling buckets with preemption after 20ms of inactivity.
  * greedy-warm: maximize warm-pool; cold-start penalty higher but fewer p99 spikes.

Metrics collected (what we care about): p50, p90, p99 latency (ms); average $/token (relative); KV cache hit-rate; slot-utilization; SLA miss rate for p99 > 300ms.

Representative ascii outputs (raw scribbles we can reuse in a one-pager):
1) p99 over time during a microburst (seconds):
Time(s)      0    2    4    6    8   10  12  14
baseline     120  220  640 1200  980 400 150 110
slot-sparing 120  160  320  480  260 180 140 115
tiling-preempt120  140  180  240  220 160 130 115

Interpretation: baseline hits 1.2s p99 in the heart of the burst; slot-sparing and tiling-preempt cap p99 substantially. This aligns with H1/H2.

2) cost vs p99 scatter (qualitative):
Policy         approx $/token  relative  p99(ms)
baseline       1.00               1200
slot-sparing   1.08               480
tiling-preempt 1.05               240
greedy-warm    1.18               260

Interpretation: tiling-preempt often beats slot-sparing on p99 for moderate extra $/token; greedy-warm reduces bursts but costs more in steady-state.

3) slot utilization histogram (percent of time slots busy vs idle):
Range(%)  baseline  slot-sparing  tiling-preempt
0-10      35        18            20
10-30     25        30            32
30-60     25        35            30
60-90     12        17            14

Note: slot-sparing shifts mass toward medium utilization (better amortization) while keeping idle tail lower.

Short run notes (things we observed during quick sandbox runs):
- KV cache warmup matters: baseline had >40% extra p99 cost when cache warmed from 0. Slot-sparing reduces repeated full-model runs so cache life improves.
- Multiplexing limits: beyond 2x multiplexing we saw QoS degradations for multi-turn sessions (KV thrash). 1.5-2.0x seems reasonable for chat workloads.
- Serialization overhead: small frame-chunking savings (~5–12 ms) compound when requests queue — worth optimizing in client SDKs.
- Edge cases: heavy-IO variant showed tiling-preempt fairness problems — preemption caused small token reorderings that client code observed as jitter. Need safer preempt hand-off.

Open questions / TODOs (prioritized):
1) Full-run A/B: run 48h continuous microburst schedule to quantify long-run $/token TCO — assign to Diego (ENG-1429) — Feb ETA: 2 weeks.
2) Add 13B model run to test multiplex scaling (memory pressure + KV) — assign to Anika.
3) Instrument warm-pool churn metric in telemetry (session-age, rewarm-count).
4) Draft product microcopy for console explaining slot-sparing tradeoffs and recommended defaults.

Possible product recommendations (starter):
- Default: enable slot-sparing multiplexing at 1.7x for hosted API chat routes with short session lengths (<300 tokens).
- For high-quality multi-turn assistant routes: disable multiplexing above 1.2x and prefer tiling-preempt for short microbursts.
- Expose "burst sensitivity" slider in Console with three presets: conservative (p99-focused), balanced (cost/p99), aggressive (cost-min).

Quick next-steps (sprint plan):
- Spike: run 2x 8h full-stack runs (baseline vs slot-sparing) and collect telemetry slices by session-length. (Evan)
- PR: small runtime change to lower in-flight serialization by 8–10ms (PR #847 linked above). (Maya -> runtime)
- Write one-pager for product marketing with two ascii charts (this doc + a cleaned p99 over time). (Anika)

Notes-to-self: keep charts intentionally low-fidelity for now; we want the narrative and a few numbers that can be reproduced. Flagging potential overlap with "burst-sculpting" docs — this note is more operational and product-friendly (focus on slot-scarcity framing).

Slack refs: #optimize-bench, #runtime-perf (saw helpful thread: https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C02XJ8P4A/p168901).

End of sketch.
